documents.content:
# Recall deployment handbook

## Staging

The staging cluster is named falcon-staging and runs in eu-west-1.
It is sized for integration tests and is rebuilt every night from the
Terraform modules in the platform-infra repository. Staging nodes use
spot instances and are allowed to restart without notice. Operators reach
staging through the bastion in the shared services account; the cluster
itself is not reachable from the public internet. Logs from staging are
retained for seven days because the environment is disposable.

## Change process

Rollbacks require two approvals from the platform team.
A normal deployment needs one approval from the service owner and a green
integration run. Deployments are frozen during the December code freeze,
and a weekly change freeze also applies every Friday after 16:00 UTC.
The on-call rotation is published every Monday in the handbook calendar.
Emergency changes may skip the review queue but still need an incident
link in the change record. Every change record must name a rollback plan.

## Storage

Postgres backups are kept for thirty days in the archive bucket.
The archive bucket is named recall-archive-2026 and lives in the same
region as production. Backups are encrypted with the platform KMS key
and restored monthly during the disaster-recovery drill. Object lifecycle
rules move backups older than thirty days to cold storage before deletion.
The restore drill is scheduled on the first Tuesday of each month.

## Production and incidents

The production cluster is named falcon-prod and runs in us-east-2.
Production nodes are spread across three availability zones and use the
graviton instance family. Cluster upgrades follow the blue-green runbook
and must be announced in the platform-ops channel one day in advance.
A sev1 incident pages the on-call engineer through Opsgenie immediately.
The incident commander opens a shared timeline within ten minutes and
posts updates every thirty minutes until the incident is resolved.
A blameless postmortem is due within five business days, and every action
item must have an owner and a due date. Customer-facing incidents also
require a status page update.
